Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session and the second innings! The West Indies players make their way out to the field and take their respective positions in the field. Sri Lanka skipper, Dimuth Karunaratne strides out with Lahiru Thirimanne to open the innings for the tourists. Kemar Roach is all set to operate with the new ball first up.
... Day 2, Afternoon session ...

So it has been a tough toil for the Sri Lankan bowlers and now the onus will be on the Sri Lankan openers to give them a solid start and the rest of the batters to give their bowlers the much-needed rest. West Indies bowlers will now look to strike early blows in the second session and put pressure on Sri Lanka. An exciting Afternoon session awaits us. Make sure you join us for that.

It was a tale of two-halves from the Sri Lankan bowlers. They bowled well for the first two sessions of Day 1 as they continued to pick wickets at regular intervals but were found wanting and out of sorts against the pair of Brathwaite and Cornwall. Take nothing away from Suranga Lakmal though. He was once again the leader and the star. Putting in a lion-hearted shift yet again and getting 4 wickets. Chameera did well for his 3 while the others all had one apiece. Sri Lanka were very indisciplined though. With Embuldeniya bowling too many no balls and the visitors were also very sloppy in the field.  Dropping three catches. And when the pitch is as flat as this one, the bowlers need extra efforts from the fielders which they did not get as much as they would have hoped for.

Brathwaite though found a very reliable partner in Cornwall. The all-rounder continued from where he left off in the bat in the first Test. He got his highest score in Tests while Brathwaite scored his first ton in almost 3 years and his first as a skipper. The duo added a 103-run stand which shifted the momentum of the game. Brathwaite and Roach then managed to frustrate the Lankans more before the tourists finally got the better of Roach. Brathwaite failed to carry the bat but his majestic 126 has taken his side to a total in excess of 350!

West Indies were put in to bat, a decision Kraigg Brathwaite himself would have done. His side though struggled to get going as Campbell and Bonner departed early on Day 1. Brathwaite stuck to the end like glue but the likes of Mayers, Blackwood, Holder, and Alzarri all failed to convert their starts. West Indies looked in all sorts of trouble at this stage struggling at 222/7 and 275 looked too much to ask for.

Finally, Sri Lanka have managed to bowl out West Indies and they have managed to do it in the first session of Day 2. The tourists though will be very disappointed as they were made to work hard to get those remaining three wickets. West Indies will be mighty pleased not just with the score but how they have kept the tourists on the park and tired them out. A brilliant knock from the West Indies skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite. His fabulous innings has put his side in a solid position.

OUT! BOWLED! CHOPPED ON! A very disappointing end to wonderful, wonderful innings by Kraigg Brathwaite. He has played a gem of an innings and gets a well-deserved standing ovation from his team-mates. Length delivery, which pitches just outside off and nips back in. Brathwaite goes for the cut shot but is cramped for room due to the inward movement. He can only get an inside edge onto his stumps. An unfortunate end to a very good knock by the skipper. WEST INDIES FINISH ON 354! WITH THAT, IT WILL ALSO BE LUNCH ON DAY 2!
That is defended solidly off the front foot.

Quicker and shorter around middle and leg, Shannon Gabriel goes back and looks to flick this one to the leg side but he misses and gets hit on the pad. An appeal is made for LBW but this one was sliding down the leg pole.
Full and tossed up on off, Shannon Gabriel prods ahead and defends the ball out.
Full and tossed up around off, driven through covers for one more. Looks like the skipper is trusting his partner to not lose his wicket here.
Shannon Gabriel gets off the mark here. Floated and on leg, Gabriel flicks this one to fine leg for a single now.

Shannon Gabriel is the last man in for the hosts.

Loopy ball, outside off. Pushed to covers.

Good length ball, on the fifth stump line. Brathwaite uses his writsts and clips this to mid-wicket.
Hits the deck on a length, just around off and Brathwaite pushes it back to Chameera.
Length ball outside off and Brathwaite defends.
FOUR! Enough of blocking, says Roach! Tossed up on off and Roach smacks it past the bowler and into the long off fence. 350 up.
Flighted ball outside off, Roach plays it to silly point.

Beaten! Flighted ball on off, Roach looks to defend but the ball spins past his bat.

Length ball on middle, Brathwaite clips this to deep square leg for a single.
Tossed up on middle, Brathwaite clips this past mid on for one.
Full ball on off, KB pushes this one to silly mid on.
Tossed up on middle, Brathwaite clips this to left of mid-wicket. But the fielder puts in a dive to stop it.

Flighted ball on off, pushed to covers.
Loopy ball on middle, Brathwaite clips it to mid on.

A touch fuller this time, on middle and leg. Roach once again, offers a solid defence.
Loopy ball on middle, Roach puts in a stride and defends it well.
Flatter ball on off, Roach defends it.

Loopy ball on leg, Roach flicks this to square leg for a single.
Tossed up ball on leg stump. Brathwaite clips it to deep mid-wicket for one.
A full ball on the line of stumps. Roach keeps it out.
Length ball on off, Roach walks across the line and defends it off the back foot.

Full ball on off, Brathwaite clips it across the line to mid on.

The pair of Rahkeem Cornwall and Kraigg Brathwaite, have continued from where they left off on Day 1 and are on the cusp of a century stand. The wicket is a flat track with nothing in it for the bowlers. The Sri Lankan bowlers have toiled hard but they need to find a way to end this stand and this innings and get some much-needed rest.
A touch fuller this time and outside off. Brathwaite shuffles across and plays it late to the man at gully.

Full ball, but wide outside off. Brathwaite knows better not to chase it.

Good length ball on middle. Brathwaite shuffles across and clips it to fine leg for a run.

Full ball on middle and Brathwaite clips this to mid-wicket for a single.
Lakmal digs this short and outside off. Cornwall goes for the pull but gets the top edge. The ball goes towards the mid-wicket region and is cut off by the man there. Single taken.
Length ball outside off. Cornwall stands tall and pushes this past covers. The fielder chases it but gives them enough time for a couple.

Too full and down the leg stump. Brathwaite looks to flick it but misses.

He seems to be in a mood to hit some boundaries! Length ball on middle, Cornwall flicks it towards the deep mid-wicket fence but the ball is cut off by the fielder. Two runs taken and that brings up 300.

Back-to-back fifties for the big man and he has played a sublime knock so far. A brilliant one, in context of the game and now, he will look to continue the same.
Hits the deck on a length, on middle. Cornwall plays this to mid on.
A touch shorter this time, on the fifth stump line. Cornwall punches this to mid off.
Length ball, outside off. Cornwall covers his stumps and offers a solid defence.

NOT OUT! Bump ball and Brathwaite is safe! A very good decision by the on-field umpire this time. Vishwa starts with a very full one, outside off. Brathwaite looks to jam it out but the ball goes back to the fielder at third slip, off the outside edge. The umpires go upstairs to check it and their soft signal is not out too, but the replay shows it is a bump ball and he is safe.

Was that a bump ball? Both the on-field umpires have a chat and decide to take this one upstairs. The soft signal is NOT OUT. One replay is enough to see that the ball bounces before going to the slip fielder. Will be NOT OUT.

FOUR! First boundary of the day and Cornwall is the one who gets it! He gets a length ball on his pads and he simply flicks it over the fielder at square leg for a boundary. The fielder was standing midway between the circle and the boundary ropes, so he couldn't get that. 5 off the opening over of the day.
A touch fuller this time, outside off and Cornwall lets it go.
Who will bowl from the other end? Vishwa Fernando, it is. 22-4-59-1 so far.

Rapped on the pads but the umpire says NOT OUT! Length ball on middle, nips in after pitching. Cornwall looks to flick but is hit on the pads. Sri Lanka appeal but the umpire is unmoved. The ball was probably sliding down leg.
Serves a length ball, on middle and Cornwall defends it solidly.

HUNDRED FOR KRAIGG BRATHWAITE! Fantastic knock from the skipper!  His first hundred as a skipper and first since July 2018! The barren spell that has been going on for almost 3 years is finally broken! This has been a skipper's knock from him. The captain has led from the front when most of his partners failed to capitalize on the starts they got. Brathwaite has been rock solid in defense and has also made sure to make the most of the loose deliveries. Brathwaite's concentration and determination in this innings has been top-notch. Gets to the landmark as he flicks this length ball to the fine leg region for a single. Now, that he has reached here, he will look to build on this and help West Indies post a big total.
Starts with a length ball, but outside off. Brathwaite offers a solid defence.

We are all in readiness for action to begin on Day 2. The batters for West Indies, skipper Kraigg Brathwaite and Rahkeem Cornwall make their way out into the middle now. Suranga Lakmal to operate with the ball first up for the visitors. Here we go...

Rahkheem Cornwall is in now for a chat! He says that he has been putting in the work in the past couple of weeks with the bat and once he gets the start, he keeps going on. Tells that they will try to continue their batting and add a hefty score to their name.

The Sri Lanka Head coach, Mickey Arthur is in for a quick chat! He says that the game is all square and the wicket did not play as expected and it was not ideal to drop those catches. Feels that they want to dismiss them quickly and bat well when they come out with the blade.

PITCH REPORT - Courtney Walsh and Darren Ganga are in for the pitch report. Ganga says that there is some grass and it is a very good pitch to bat on. Adds that Kraigg showed real patience and scored runs down the ground and on the leg side too, which is what the batters should look to do. Walsh says that there is a little bit of swing and reverse swing will come into play. Further adds that if the bowlers bowl in the right areas, then they can do well and the spinners should look to bowl quicker.

West Indies, on the other hand, are amidst a very good stand between Brathwaite and Cornwall. The pair managed to pull things back in their favor in the last session and will be looking to continue that good work. The skipper is a run away from getting his first ton in three years and he'd look to first achieve that and then put his side in a stronger position. A very exciting day awaits us. Who will this day belong to?

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the second and final Test between West Indies and Sri Lanka. The tourists were very good for the majority of Day 1 but they lost the plot in the final session which might prove to be costly. Sri Lanka will hope to correct those wrongs and first try to wrap up West Indies' innings in the first innings and then put on a show with the bat.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Right then! West Indies are still in a strong position despite not starting strongly. Their skipper will have to wait for the day to bring up his ton as he ended on 99. Sri Lanka would rue the dropped chances which robbed them of bowling West Indies out on a lower score. They would though hope that they come back refreshed on Day 2 and take the remaining three wickets quickly and then play a good long inning with the bat. Who will take the honors on Day 2? Join us on 30th March 2021 at 1000 local (1400 GMT). Till then, take care and cheers.

Kraigg Brathwaite is in for a quick chat! He says that he just wanted to play the ball as late as possible. Adds that Sri Lanka are a good bowling unit and he looked to be disciplined. Feels that they lost 2 wickets more than wanted but it is a good score and says that the first session of Day 2 will be important.

For Sri Lanka, Suranga Lakmal started superbly by picking two quick wickets at the start of the game, and the other bowlers too bowled brilliantly. But Lakmal was the star performer for them as he took 3 wickets. Fernando, Chameera, Embuldeniya, and de Silva all had a wicket to their name too. They though would rue their sloppy fielding as they dropped at least 4 catches, one of which was of that of the West Indian skipper which came to haunt them later in the day. Embuldeniya had a tough day with the ball as he bowled a lot of No Balls which is not expected from a spinner. Overall, they would be happy with their bowling but would love to improve their fielding cometh day two.

After being asked to bat first, West Indies faltered as they were jolted early losing Campbell and Bonner without much on the board. Though Mayers joined hands with his skipper, Braithwaite to stage a 71-run association to take them into Lunch. West Indies then lost Mayers in the first over after Lunch but Blackwood counterattacked along with his skipper to keep the score moving and keeping the Lankan bowlers at bay. He though could not continue for long as he departed to a rash shot. Then the partnership of 51 runs between Holder and Brathwaite revived them again. Though the story to throw away starts continued as Holder became the latest victim as he departed just at the stroke of Tea. Joseph too played a cameo but he too could not last long and then Cornwall with his controlled aggression stitched a 50+ stand as his skipper remained unbeaten on 99 at the close of play. Had the fielder not dropped Brathwaite when he was in the 20s, Sri Lanka would have ended up bowling West Indies out.

A brilliant opening day of a Test match where there was a good contest between the bat and ball. After putting the host to bat, Sri Lanka just ran riot in the opposition camp as they reduced them down to 7 wickets. Though West Indies would take a leaf out of the book of their captain who fought hard the whole day to take West Indies to a good score, so far. A sheer entertaining day to set up the next 4 days of the Test.

NOT OUT! A scare at the very last ball of the day but Rahkeem Cornwall survives. A length ball around middle and leg, Cornwall looks to flick this one to the leg side but he misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal is made but the umpire shakes his head. This time, the Sri Lankan skipper, Dimuth Karunaratne makes the 'T' symbol rather quickly. Maybe he thinks that this is close. Ultra Edge shows no bat. Ball Tracker shows to be the Umpire's Call on the wickets. Sri Lanka retain their review and Rahkeem Cornwall does not lose his wicket. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1!

Review time! Sri Lanka take the review for the LBW against Rahkeem Cornwall. The replays roll in and the Ultra Edge comes on and shows that there is no bat involved. Ball Tracker shows that it is Umpire's Call on hitting the wickets.
Around off, on a good length, coming back in with the angle, Rahkeem Cornwall shows the full face of the blade and offers a secure defense.
He moves onto 99 now! A back of a length ball, on the pads, Kraigg Brathwaite clips this one to fine leg for a single.
Fuller on leg, whipped to the square leg fielder. Kraigg Brathwaite is loud as he says no to the single, to Rahkeem Cornwall.
Around off on a length, worked through square leg for a single. Now then, up comes Kraigg Brathwaite on strike and he is on 98 too!
Angling in a length ball on off, Cornwall pushes this one to the point region.

Leg bye. Length ball on the pads, Rahkeem Cornwall looks to flick but he misses and the ball takes the pad and goes to the on side. The batters take the leg bye.
The skipper of West Indies has now reached 98! He also has scored 4000 runs in Test cricket for West Indies and he will be happy with this feat. Around off, worked to mid-wicket for a single.

On a good length and outside off, the ball is nipping away from Cornwall as he lets the ball through to the keeper.

A carbon copy of the previous delivery.

Short and around off, Cornwall crunches the drive but straight to cover-point.
As expected, Vishwa Fernando (19-4-50-1) will steam in from the other end.
Length and outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, teasing the batsman to go after it. Kraigg holds himself back as he lets it go through to the keeper.
Short of a good length around off, KB defends it out off he back foot.
Fuller and around off, Kraigg blocks it out to the leg side.
Full and outside off, squeezed to point.

On middle, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.

A session where the Sri Lankans stamped their authority and have bowled well to snare 3 more wickets in this session and have pushed the hosts on the back foot. Kyle Mayers and Kraigg Brathwaite were looking good in the 1st session but Mayers was sent back, in the first over, after Lunch. Blackwood came out and was showing attacking intent, but once again, it did not last long and he was back to the shed too. Then, came a good stand between Jason Holder and skipper, Brathwaite as they stitched a 51-run stand, and also where the skipper reached his half-ton, which he has absolutely deserved. Just at the stroke of Tea, Holder gifted his wicket away too. Three different bowlers snared wickets for the Lankans, but all of them have bowled well and will look to do the same after the Tea break. Will they be able to do so? Or will the captain and Da Silva stitch a big stand? Join us shortly to find out.

This time, Blackwood was not in two minds. A bouncer on middle, Jermaine Blackwood just sways away like in the movie Matrix and lets the ball zip through, to the keeper.
PLAY AND A MISS! Looked to play it really late but he misses out here. A slow bouncer outside off, Jermaine Blackwood is in two minds and finally decides to play the upper cut. Misses though.

On a good length, angling around middle and leg, Jermaine Blackwood looks to work this one to the on side but he missed and wears a blow to the pad. Another appeal but the umpire is as still as a statue.

On a much fuller length and on the middle pole, Kraigg Brathwaite clips this one through mid-wicket. The man in the deep runs to his left and does well to pull the ball back to his partner. Saves a run for his team.

FOUR! The skipper is playing some really eye catching strokes. Sweet shot, this! On a good length and around off, Kraigg Brathwaite just packs a punch through the mid off region and the ball runs away to the ropes.
Around off on a length, pushed to the mid on region.
Dushmantha Chameera is back on.
Good length and in the channel around off, Blackwood decides not to play at it.
And beaten again! Good length and angled around off, Blackwood prods forward in defence but the ball goes past his outside edge again this time.
Play and a miss again! Length and well outside off, Jermaine once again looks to power it through the off side but misses all ends up there.
Swing and a miss! Length and angled outside off, Blackwood chases at it but is beaten on the outside edge.
Good length and around off, Blackwood is solid in defence off the front foot.

NOT OUT! The inside edge saves Blackwood there! Length and angled on middle, Jermaine looks to work it to the leg side but gets beaten to wear the blow on the pads. There is a strong appeal from the bowler but the umpire is unmoved. Karunaratne takes the review. The Ultra Edge comes on and detects a spike when the ball is close to the bat. Sri Lanka lose a review.

Review time! This is for LBW! Dimuth Karunaratne has a quick chat and then decides to make the 'T' symbol. First, Ultra Edge comes and clearly, you can see that there is a SPIKE as the ball goes by the bat. Sri Lanka lose their review here.
Angling on a length and around off, Brathwaite defends it out.
On off, played back to the bowler.
Full on off, pushed down to the leg side.
Short of a length on middle, Blackwood tucks it to square leg for a single.

An appeal for LBW but turned down! Length and angled on leg, Jermaine looks to tuck it to the leg side but gets beaten to get rapped on the thigh pad. Lakmal makes a stifled appeal but the umpire turns it down.
FOUR! Blackwood in ODI mode! Full and angled on middle, Blackwood lofts it through mid-wicket with ease to get a boundary.
Good length and around off, Kraigg defends it to the off side.
Length ball around off, Brathwaite keeps it out.
On off, Kraigg blocks it out.

EDGED AND FOUR! Once again the outside edge is found and again the ball runs to the fence! Length and angling away from Brathwaite. Kraigg looks to defend it but the ball brushes the outside edge and runs past gully for a boundary at third man.
Length and around off, Kraigg blocked it to covers.
Length and around off, Brathwaite comes on the front foot and then makes a leave.
Full and down leg, Blackwood looks to clip it fine but misses it as Dickwella dives to his left to pouch it.
Full and on leg, tucked away to the leg side.
SIX! That's gone the distance! Length and around off, Blackwood goes downtown and connects well to send the ball sailing over long off for a biggie.
Length and around off, Blackwood looks to defend it off the back foot but gets squared up slightly as he fends it to the off side.
FOUR! Smashed! Full and around off, Blackwood frees his arms and hits it through the line past mid off for a boundary at long off.
Length and around off, Blackwood defends it off the front foot.
Short of a length and around leg, Blackwood pulls it to deep square leg for a single to get off the mark.  A brilliant over from Fernando there.
Who will bowl from the other end? Sri Lankans' man of the first session, Suranga Lakmal is going to lead the attack from the other end. 10-6-25-2 so far.
Good length and around off, defended off the front foot.
Length and around leg, Blackwood blocks it down to mid on.
Jermaine Blackwood is the new man in with the bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! A good delivery from Fernando and a brilliant take from Dickwella. Vishwa bowls a full ball outside off, Mayers who was batting on 49 sees it as a scoring opportunity as he goes for the drive but without any footwork. The ball though swings a hint away to catch the outside edge and fly to the keeper who dives to his left to take the grab.  The umpire though does not give it instantly as he seeks the help of the third umpire. The Third umpire after looking at a few replays rules that Kyle Mayers is out.

The umpires converge and send the caught behind decision upstairs! The soft signal is out. It is a fair delivery as the replays roll in. The third umpire checks for bump ball but it is not to be.  The keeper too has taken the catch cleanly and Mayers has to depart. An early blow for West Indies again after the break.
Another good length ball around off, Mayers is not interested to play at it.
Fernando starts with a length ball and it is outside off, Mayers lets it be.

Welcome back to the post Lunch Session. The Sri Lankan players are out on the field as the two West Indian batsmen, Kraigg Brathwaite and Kyle Mayers resume their innings too. Vishwa Fernando to start with the ball in this session.
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Right then! West Indies would look to build on the start they have got with Brathwaite and Mayers to help them post a good first innings total. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, would look to pick up regular wickets to keep the West Indies scoring in check. Who will take the second session? Join us to find out at 1240 local (1640 GMT).

Sri Lanka would be a lot happier with their start with the ball. Lakmal and Fernando began on the right note as they bowled probing lines and lengths. Though Fernando could not get a wicket, Lakmal was very successful as he took a couple of wickets to hand the early advantage to the visitors. Chameera and Embuldeniya too bowled well but Sri Lanka could not manage to get another breakthrough before the Lunch break.

Put in to bat, West Indies openers began on a watchful note but they could not stitch a stand which they would have expected as Campbell was sent packing. Lakmal again struck when he had the centurion from the last game, Nkrumah Bonner who edged one onto the stumps. Since that wicket, Mayers played his natural game as he found boundaries but also edged a few which dropped short of a fielder or the fielder dropped one. Despite all this Brathwaite and Mayers stood strong as they stitched a 71-run stand to bring the West Indian innings back on track as they head into Lunch without any further damage.

A brilliant session from Sri Lanka. Lakmal justified his captain's decision to bowl first by taking two quick wickets as he made the West Indian batsmen dance to his tunes. But credit should go to the West Indies too as their skipper has looked good so far and Mayers who is out there to partner his skipper has fought hard.
On a good length and on off, Kraigg Brathwaite comes ahead and keeps the ball out nicely. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Closer to the off pole but on a length. Still not enough for Kraigg Brathwaite to play at this and another leave.
Surprise, surprise! First bumper of the day from Dushmantha Chameera. This one is outside off and hence, easier for Kraigg Brathwaite to just leave it alone.
On a good length and outside off, punched to covers this time.
Around off, back of a length, KB hops and looks to help the ball to the on side. Misses and gets hit high on the thigh pad.
Good length outside off, left alone.

FOUR! A beautiful stroke from Mayers. On a good length this time, outside off, there is width for Kyle to play with and he punches this one with authority through cover-point and into the ropes. 8 runs off the over.
PLAY AND A MISS! A fuller ball, way outside off, the ball hits the deck and nips away and Kyle Mayers gets low and looks to work this one through covers. He misses again.
Short of a length and around off, Kyle Mayers pulls this one, although not in the cleanest of manners, over the mid on fielder for a couple of runs.
Fuller this time around the off pole, KB strokes this one to the mid off region for a single.
BEATEN! Beautifully bowled. Slants in a length ball across the right-hander, Kraigg Brathwaite gets his bat, looking to have a feel of the ball. He misses his stroke though.

Leg bye. Angles in a length ball around middle and leg, Kyle Mayers looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads, and the ball goes to the square leg region. The batters take the leg bye this time.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
On a good length and outside off, Kraigg Brathwaite leaves this one be.
Fuller on off, Kraigg works this one to the mid on region.
Around off again, on a length this time, Kyle pushes this one through point and crosses over with a single.
Same length but closer to the off pole this time, Mayers pushes this one to the on side.
Short of a length and around off, punched to the cover region this time.
On a good length and around off, Kraigg Brathwaite pushes the ball back to the bowler.
Back of a length and on the pads, Kraigg Brathwaite hops and tucks this one to square leg.
Outside off, on a good length, left alone.
Around leg, KB looks to tuck it but he misses and gets rapped on the pad.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Vishwa Fernando is back on.

An appeal for caught behind but the umpire turns this one down. A back of a length ball around off, coming back into Kraigg, as he looks to tuck it away. He seems to have missed it and the ball takes the thigh pad and goes to the keeper. An appeal but nothing from the umpire. No review taken too. A good decision by Dimuth Karunaratne as replays show that there was no bat on this.
Length and around off, Mayers strokes it firmly but cannot beat the man at mid off.
EDGED AND SHORT AGAIN! Short of a good length and across Mayers, Kyle looks to defend it but gets an outside edge which flies towards third slip where it falls agonisingly short of the fielder there.
Fuller and around off, Mayers goes for the drive again but gets it off the inner half of the bat through wide mid on. The ball get a brace there.

FOUR! Another edge goes for a boundary! A short of a length ball around off, Mayers is on the back foot as he looks to defend it but he ends up getting a thick outside edge which flies through the gully region. The ball runs to the third man fence for a boundary.
Short of a length ball around off, Mayers looks to pull but is beaten there.
FOUR! Powerful shot down the ground! Kyle Mayers at his best! Full and around off, Mayers leans into the drive and then strokes it through mid off for a boundary.
Full and on leg, tucked towards the leg side. A good first over from Dhananjaya de Silva.
On middle, turned to the leg side.
Flighted around off, Kraigg blocks it away.
Flatter around off, Brathwaite punches it off the back foot this time.
Another tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Loopy on off, Kraigg blocks it off the front foot.
Dhananjaya de Silva is into the attack now.
Good length and around off, Mayers blocks it out.
Full and leaving Mayers again, Kyle goes after it and slices it high up in the air towards long off. He though cannot get the boundary but manages to get two runs.
Length and around off, Mayers punches the ball off the back foot to covers.
Another length ball going away from Mayers as Kyle once again goes for an expansive drive but fails to get the connection right. He gets beaten on the outside edge.
Swing and a miss! Length ball leaving the left-hander there, Mayers goes chasng after it but is lucky to not have edged that. Could have left that alone.
Full on middle, Brathwaite looks to clip it but he gets it off the pads to the elg side a leg bye taken. 50-run stand is also up between these two.
Dushmantha Chameera into the attack for the first time in this Test.
On the middle pole, flicked to the square leg region.
FOUR! Another boundary for the left-hander! Nicely played. Flatter and outside off, width on offer and so he backs away and punches this one through cover-point.
Flatter and on middle, well defended out, off the back foot by Kyle.
Short and around off, cut away through covers for a single.
Full and tossed up again around off, Kraigg defends.
Full and tossed up on off, KB does well to dig the ball out.
Around off, on a length, blocked to covers. 8 runs off the over.
FOUR! Overpitched around off, Kyle Mayers plays this uppishly, but through the gap at mid off and the ball speeds away to the ropes.
On a good length around off, seaming back into the left-hander, Kyle Mayers looks to play at this one but he misses and the ball goes to Niroshan Dickwella.
Around off, played to the off side for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
On a good length and around off, punched through covers for three this time.
On off, defended.
On off, pushed to the off side for a single now.
On off, pushed through covers for a single.
Around off, blocked out. No ball called as Lasith Embuldeniya had overstepped.
Shortish and on off, Mayers goes on the back foot and bunts this one through mid on. Rotates the strike.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Full and tossed up around off, Kyle blocks this one to the short leg fielder.
Angled into the middle pole on a length, worked through square leg for a single.
On a good length and outside off, Kyle shuffles across the off stump slightly and makes a leave.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.

An appeal for LBW but this is turned down. On a good length and outside off, the ball seams back in sharply into the left-hander as Kyle swings his blade at this, to the leg side but he misses. Gets rapped high on the pad and and there is an appeal. Nothing from the umpire.
Around off, on a good length, played with soft hands, with the outer half of the blade, to the gully fielder.
On a good length outside off, Kyle looks to punch this one, off the back foot, through covers, but he misses his stroke.
Around off, worked through point for a single to see off the over.
Same line and length, Kyle goes on the back foot and defends this one to the left of the bowler.
Flatter on off again, punched to the mid off fielder.
Short and around off, tapped to the cover region this time by Mayers.
On middle, nudged to short leg.
Flighted on off, Mayers looks to defend but the ball spins in and bounces too as he misses and gets hit high on the pad.
Fuller and around off and middle, Kraigg strokes it down to mid on to see off the over.
Length ball outside off, Brathwaite is happy to make a leave there.

Good length and outside off, Mayers stands tall and then just punches it through point. There is no timing on the shot and hence the ball won't reach the fence. Despite that, the batsmen manage to take three valuable runs.
And again a leave as the ball is again on a length but it is outside off so no issues for Mayers to shoulder arms to it.
Another length ball but the line is outside off and Mayers is not going to after it at this stage of the game.
Length and around off, left alone by Mayers.
On middle, worked to the fielder at short leg. Good comeback from Lasith Embuldeniya after going for 10 runs in his first over.
Fuller on off, driven through to covers.
Loopy on off, Kraigg presses forward in defence.
Outside off, left alone.
Loopy on off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Floated on off, blocked off the front foot.
Length and around off, Mayers punches it off the back foot to mid on.

DRINKS! This has been a very strong start to the game by the visitors. It has been all about Suranga Lakmal as he has been terrorizing the West Indian batters and also has 2 wickets to his name. He has been getting the outside edges too, 3 so far, but they have either run away through vacant gaps, to the boundary or have been dropped. Sri Lanka will look for more of the same and the hosts, would be looking at Kraigg and Mayers to hang on, until the Lunch break atleast.
Length and around off, Kyle strokes it to gully.

EDGED AND DROPPED! This should have been taken! Length and around off, Mayers again looks to defend it but ekes out a thick outside edge off the back foot. The ball flies to the left of the third slip fielder where Pathum Nissanka dives early to spill the chance there.

EDGED AND FOUR! Three edges and three boundaries! Length and around off, Mayers is squared up on defence as he manages to get a thick outside edge which flies in between the third slip and gully to run to the fence at third man for a boundary.
FOUR! Muscular hit! Full and around off, Mayers comes on the front foot and then lofts it over mid on as the ball runs away to the long on fence for a boundary.
Good length and around off, Mayers looks to clip it to the leg side but gets beaten to take the blow on the pads. Called a No Ball as Suranga Lakmal had overstepped.

FOUR! Edged and lucky boundary there! Length and coming in with the angle, Mayers looks to leave it but he is late to do so. The ball takes the inside edge and runs past the stumps and towards fine leg fence for a boundary.
Outside off, defended to covers.
Short and around off, blocked away.
On off, blocked out.
Flatter and outside off, Kraigg cuts it through cover-point for a brace.
FOUR! Now on the other side of the wicket! Flatter and around off, Brathwaite rocks on the back foot and then cuts it through point. The ball has enough legs to beat the chasing fielder to the fence.
FOUR! Easily clipped away! Fuller and around leg, Brathwaite leans and then clips it through mid-wicket for fetch a boundary.
Full and outside off, left alone by Mayers there. 6th consecutive maiden from Suranga Lakmal.
First change of the morning. Time for some spin as Lasith Embuldeniya is getting ready to bowl.
Another length ball in line with the stumps and Mayers blocks it out.

Huge appeal from Lakmal for LBW but not given by the umpire. Full and tailing into Mayers there, Kyle looks to clip it to the leg side but gets beaten to wear the blow on the pads. Lakmal appeals but just mere shake of the head from the umpire. Going down leg seems to be.
This time Suranga lands one on a length and around off and gets the ball to tail into Mayers. Kyle is hurried onto it as he fends it out to the leg side.
Lakmal is asking all sorts of questions! Length and around off again, Mayers is on the back foot as he tentatively pokes at it but gets beaten on the outside edge again.
BEATEN! Length and around off, Mayers looks to poke at it off the back foot but he gets beaten on the outside edge. He was in two minds whether to play it or leave it.
A carbon copy of the previous delivery.
In the channel of uncertainty outside off, KB knows better and just leaves it be.
Short of a length ball around off, KB taps this one to the point region.
Outside off, no shot offered.

FOUR! Another boundary for Kraigg Brathwaite and he is playing his strokes here. A length ball on middle, swinging into the right-hander and is around leg, by the time it reaches the batter. Kraigg Brathwaite just tickles this one to the fine leg fence.
Around off, length, defended to covers.
Kyle Mayers is the new man in with the bat. West Indies in some early trouble with the bat there.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Unlucky for Bonner but Lakmal gets his second scalp of the day. The centurion of the last game goes back for a duck and he will be very unhappy with his display here. Around off, on a good length, Nkrumah Bonner gets his bat across, possibly looking to defend. The ball shapes back into the right-hander, takes the inside edge and goes onto crash into the furniture behind.
Length around off, Bonner comes ahead looking to defend, but the ball shapes away at the last moment and goes by, without feeling the outside edge and goes to the keeper.

Edged...short! It Falls short of the fielder and Bonner has been handed an early scare. On a good length, around off, Nkrumah Bonner comes ahead, looking to block this one but the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards the second slip fielder, where the fielder comes ahead but the ball drops in front of him.
On middle, on a length, blocked out.
A fuller ball on middle and leg, Bonner looks to play at this but misses and gets hit on the pad. An appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Looked to be missing leg, this one.
Around off, defended.

FOUR! Just a gentle push this time, for the boundary. On a good length and around off, Kraigg Brathwaite stands tall and pushes this one through mid off. The ball finds its way to the ropes in the deep. A boundary to end the over.
Fuller delivery, almost yorker length on middle, blocked out by Kraigg.
Back of a length and on middle, nudged to the mid-wicket region.
Fuller on off, pushed away to covers.
Back of a length and around off, KB just leaves this one.
Around middle, played towards covers.
Who comes out to bat now? Nkrumah Bonner is the new man in. He was the one who held West Indies innings to eke out a draw. Can he do it again?

OUT! TAKEN! Finally he strikes and Campbell goes back for a low score. Beautifully bowled by Lakmal and the first wicket has been snared very early on by the Lankans. In Suranga Lakmal's last over too, John Campbell had edged one too but the catch was not taken. Now, it has been gobbled up by Niroshan Dickwella. On a good length, around the off pole, the ball holds the line as John Campbell comes ahead, looking to block. All he manages to do is induce an outside edge, which the keeper, Niroshan Dickwella takes nicely.
Angles in a length delivery around off, Campdell shows the full face of the bat and blocks this to the off side.
Angling into the pads on a length, John flicks this one to the leg slip fielder.
An action replay of the previous ball.
A length delivery but this one is outside off, no problems for John as he makes a leave.
On middle, nudged to the mid-wicket region.

FOUR! Very well played and the timing on this one was sublime. In fact, so sublime that even though there were two fielders who gave it a chase, the ball won the race to the ropes. On a good length around off again, Kraigg Brathwaite whips this one through mid-wicket and fetches a boundary.
Now comes 'round the wicket and bowls a length ball on off, KB manages to come ahead and defend the ball, to the man stationed at mid on.
Outside off, left alone.
Fuller, but on leg, Kraigg Brathwaite clips this one to the man at square leg. They do not go for the single on this occasion.
Short of a length but closer to the off pole this time, Kraigg Brathwaite judges this one well, to leave it, in the end. Good bounce and carry to the keeper.
On a good length and around off, Kraigg pushes the ball to the mid off region.

EDGED AND JUST SHORT! Lovely piece of bowling from Lakmal there. He kept on probing that off stump line and gets Campbell to push it off the back foot this time. The ball though shapes away a hint to catch the outside edge but John played it with soft hands. The ball flew to the fielder at gully but it fell well short of Oshada Fernando there who does well to parry the ball to the slip region.
Length and around off, coming into the batsman there. John defends it off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
Fuller and around off, Campbell comes on the front foot and then defend the ball to the off side.
Short of good length and around off, Campbell hops and plays the ball to point this time.
Length and around off, John blocks it to the leg side off the back foot.
Back of a length ball around off, Campbell looks to clip it to the leg side but is beaten by the extra bounce to get rapped on the thigh pad. The ball rolls to the off side.
Length delivery on leg but swinging down in the end. Brathwaite looks to clip it fine by getting inside the line but is beaten. The keeper, Niroshan Dickwella dives to his left to collect the ball.
Fuller and a bit around off, Kraigg comes down the wicket to cater to the movement as he strokes it to covers.
Length and around off, Kraigg defends it out off the front foot and towards the bowler.
Fuller in length and around off, Brathwaite blocks it out to the off side.
Short of good length and around off, Campbell hops inside the crease before pushing it to cover-point for a quick single.
Fuller in length and around off, Campbell comes on the front foot as he defends it out.
A bit of swing and shape there! On a good length and well outside off, it is not in Brathwaite's playing zone as he allows the ball to go and settle into the mitts of the keeper.
Short and around off, Kraigg rocks on the back foot and then pushes it towards mid off.
Fuller and outside off, Brathwaite shoulders arms to this one.
Short of a length ball around off, Brathwaite blocks it off the back foot to covers.
Fuller and around off, Kraigg prods forward and strokes it to covers.
On a good length and outside off, Brathwaite does not have any fuss in leaving this one.
Length and outside off, Campbell watches the ball and then makes a leave.
Length and around off, John blocks it off the back foot.
FOUR! Extravagantly driven! Full and around off, Campbell comes on the front foot as his eyes lit up on the scoring opportunity. He leans and strokes the drive through covers for a boundary.
Lovely inswinger! Length and angled on middle and leg, Campbell looks to tuck it to the leg side but he misses it to get rapped on the pads. Fernando appeals but the umpire is unmoved.
On a good length and outside off, John makes a leave.
Good length and around off, Campbell stays on the back foot to punch it to the bowler.
Good length and outside off, Kraigg watches it and then makes a leave.
Campbell is underway too! Length and sliding down leg, John looks to leave it but the ball takes the thigh pad and goes to the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Who will partner Lakmal with the new cherry? As expected, Vishwa Fernando to bowl from the other end.
Lands one closer on off and gets it to tail into Campbell. John is solid off the back foot too.
Another length delivery around off, John is solid in defense once again on the front foot.
Good length and around off, Campbell comes on the front foot and then blocks it out staunchly.

Kraigg Brathwaite and West Indies are underway! Courtesy of a leg bye. Lakmal starts one on a fuller length but it is sliding onto the pads. Kraigg looks to clip it to the leg side but the ball goes off his pads to fine leg. A leg bye taken.

We are all set to begin after the pre-match formalities.  The Sri Lankan players are out there in the middle, followed by the two West Indian openers, John Campbell and Kraigg Braithwaite. Suranga Lakmal to start with the ball. Here we go...

Lahiru Thirimanne is down for the chat. He says that it is about being patient in the middle. Says that he has been able to do so in the last 2 series. Adds that he is really impressed with the young fast bowlers and batters in the team. Praises Nissanka for a good show in the last game. Tells that he is looking forward to the next couple of series.

Nkrumah Bonner is in for a quick chat! He says that it is good to get the first hundred in Test cricket and his focus is on this game now. States that batting at Number 3 is an honor for him. Tells that he does not know a lot about the deck today and their focus is always on winning the game.

Pitch Report - Samuel Badree and Sir Curtley Ambrose are down for the Pitch Report.  Badree says the heavy roller was used and that has helped the surface to get compacted. He further says that the outfield is superb and the batsmen will fetch runs for their shots. Sir Curtley Ambrose says that it is a different surface and there is dry grass on it. He also says that there will be bounce and early on before the pitch settles out and becomes good for batting.

West Indies skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite says that they would have bat anyways. He says that there is less moisture than in the last game. He mentions that the key is discipline and it is a mixture of good batting and bowling but the main thing is discipline. He also says that they are going unchanged and the experienced players in the team give us a lot of inspiration but again he says that being disciplined is the key here.

Dimuth Karunaratne, the Sri Lanka captain, says that they will bowl first. Adds that there is moisture underneath the deck and they want to make the most of the advantage from their pacers. Informs that they are unchanged. Tells that they have a very good chance to beat West Indies and they will battle it out session-by-session.

Sri Lanka (Unchanged Playing XI) - Dimuth Karunaratne (C), Lahiru Thirimanne, Oshada Fernando, Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya de Silva, Pathum Nissanka, Niroshan Dickwella (WK), Suranga Lakmal, Dushmantha Chameera, Lasith Embuldeniya, Vishwa Fernando.

West Indies (Unchanged Playing XI) - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), John Campbell, Nkrumah Bonner, Kyle Mayers, Jermaine Blackwood, Jason Holder, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Rahkeem Cornwall, Alzarri Joseph, Kemar Roach, Shannon Gabriel.
TOSS - Sri Lanka have won the toss and have decided to BOWL first.

Hello and a warm welcome one and all to the coverage of the 2nd Test between both the Island nations, West Indies and Sri Lanka. The first Test was a 5-day thriller, which we don't really see these days in Test cricket and that was a welcome surprise, indeed. Both the teams fought tooth and nail and at the end of the day, no one could be pronounced as the winner. Heading into the second Test, both teams will be high on confidence as they have demonstrated that they both have the tools in their arsenal, to trump the other. It will just be about the application and intent shown and which teams want it more. Will we see a winner in this clash? Or will we have another entertaining game, but a game that ends in the honours being shared? All the answers coming your way, with the toss and team news first.
